messages.author: a7efa9b556a70ea4
messages.subject: error using INLA in R 3.2.1
parts:
Hi, 

I'm trying to run INLA on a spate-temporal model, and finally seemed to get the code working until I encountered the following error:

> model.inla.ST<-inla(formula.ST,family="poisson",data=studygroup)
dyld: Library not loaded: /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/3.3/Resources/lib/libR.dylib
  Referenced from: /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/3.2/Resources/library/INLA/bin/mac/64bit/inla
  Reason: Incompatible library version: inla requires version 3.3.0 or later, but libR.dylib provides version 3.2.0
sh: line 1: 33695 Trace/BPT trap: 5       '/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/3.2/Resources/library/INLA/bin/mac/64bit/inla.run' -b -s -v '/var/folders/sm/p7dyr78d285_lp0h5grrgcgr0000gn/T//RtmpYvnnzk/file7727393f63d0/Model.ini' > /var/folders/sm/p7dyr78d285_lp0h5grrgcgr0000gn/T//RtmpYvnnzk/file7727393f63d0/Logfile.txt
Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed() : 
  The inla-program exited with an error. Unless you interupted it yourself, please rerun with verbose=TRUE and check the output carefully.
  If this does not help, please contact the developers at <he...@r-inla.org>.

Now, I've tried updating R to the latest version to see if this would solve the problem.  Unfortunately, I then ran into several more problems with other packages I needed for my code, as they did not appear to be updated yet for the latest version of R.  In particular, spdep did not want to even install in R 3.3.1.  So I never found my way to seeing if R 3.3.1 would solve my INLA issue.  However, I happen to know that others are able to get INLA to work using R 3.2.1 without issue, so I am hoping to also get it to run this way.  If anyone has any suggestions that might help it run, that would be great.

Best,
Jesse
